claims.text: Inflammatory bowel disease affects approximately 7 million people worldwide [^src1]
Approximately 70,000 Danes have inflammatory bowel disease, corresponding to approximately 1% of the population [^src1]
IBD most commonly develops in individuals aged 20-40 years [^src1]
The incidence of IBD is increasing globally [^src1]
Colorectal cancer remains one of the most common causes of death among IBD patients [^src1]
Surveillance colonoscopies result in early diagnosis of colorectal cancer and improved survival [^src1]
There is strong evidence and broad international agreement for offering all PSC patients annual systematic follow-up with colonoscopy [^src1]
The development target for PSC colonoscopy surveillance is that 80% of patients receive colonoscopy within 18 months [^src1]
Nationally, 81% of PSC patients received colonoscopy within 18 months during the period 01.10.2023 - 30.09.2024, meeting the development target of at least 80% [^src1]
A total of 345 PSC patients were monitored during the period, of which 31 were newly diagnosed [^src1]
PSC patients are most often men (68%) with an average age of 46 years [^src1]
All five regions achieved results meeting the development target of at least 80% for PSC colonoscopy surveillance [^src1]
Regional variation in PSC colonoscopy completion rates ranges from 79% to 85% [^src1]
Among the eight departments with more than 10 PSC patients, department variation in colonoscopy completion rates ranges from 76% to 95% [^src1]
SUH Køge Medicin improved its PSC colonoscopy completion rate by 9 percentage points compared to the previous year [^src1]
In 65% of performed colonoscopies for PSC surveillance, biopsies were taken [^src1]
All PSC surveillance colonoscopies were performed in hospital settings [^src1]

The steering group assesses that the re-operation rate is generally too high, with variation of 11-15% between regions excluding Region Sjælland, but with large variation between individual departments [^src1]
The steering group encourages internal audit at departments with high re-operation rates [^src1]
The development target for re-operation rate is assessed as still relevant at 8% [^src1]
The steering group is concerned about whether all PSC patients are coded correctly and encourages departments to address this issue [^src1]
The development target for PSC colonoscopy surveillance is assessed as still relevant [^src1]

timeline.event: Monitoring period for PSC colonoscopy surveillance indicator, during which 345 PSC patients were monitored with 81% receiving colonoscopy within 18 months

context: This chunk describes the disease area of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and the quality measurement framework of DANIBD, focusing on Indicator 7 regarding primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) surveillance. The document establishes that IBD affects approximately 70,000 Danes and 7 million people worldwide, with colorectal cancer being a major cause of death among IBD patients. The chunk presents detailed results from the 2023-2024 monitoring period showing that 81% of PSC patients nationally received colonoscopy surveillance within 18 months, meeting the 80% development target across all five Danish regions. The broader narrative contextualizes DANIBD's role in monitoring and improving IBD treatment quality across Danish hospital departments through evidence-based indicators developed by the steering group in collaboration with professional societies and the independent Danish medical council.
